free_tier.stated: 1 GiB PER FILE in the project *file release* area - a separate, much smaller surface than the PPA. The manual says: 'Each individual file must be no more than 1 GiB and you must be the: project maintainer / project driver / or the series release manager.' There is no published total-per-project cap; the unit of accounting is the individual release file. (The 8 GiB figure widely quoted for Launchpad is the PPA disk quota - it does not govern file releases.)

egress.terms: Free, no billing. Files are served from launchpadlibrarian.net behind a 303 redirect. No published transfer cap; a measured ~70 KB/s single-stream on a PPA .deb is a throughput problem rather than a quota one.

tooling: Web upload per release ('Add download file') is the documented path - no SFTP/rsync equivalent to Savannah or SourceForge for the release area. Automation goes through the Launchpad web service API: `launchpadlib` (Python), the `+download` URL shape, and hardware-bound API tokens. Consumer side is plain HTTPS GET with an MD5 and optional GPG signature per file.
chaining: unlimited projects x unlimited series x unlimited releases x 1 GiB per file. At 1 GiB granularity 500 GB is 500 files - feasible but operationally noisy, and every upload is a web action unless scripted via launchpadlib. Distinct from the PPA path (8 GiB/PPA, .deb-only, dput/rsync upload).
limits_note: per-object-cap: 1 GiB hard per release file. extras.agent_focus: The code-forge seam: OSS project hosts, software-download directories, game/mod distribution and mirror services. Question for each: (a) any published byte quota, (b) is upload possible over SFTP/rsync/SCP/SSH rather than a web form, (c) is there a public download CDN, (d) does it need an approved project or can any account create one, (e) per-file cap. Round 2 flagged that SourceForge has no published quota and serves over plain SFTP with a global mirror CDN, and that an rclone-backend enumerator would score the niche as empty. This slot tests that class systematically. Every number below was read live or from a dated archive capture this session.

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
